analysis.title: The Point for North America, Wednesday, 28 October 2026
key_insights: Boeing 3Q26 adj. EPS was -$0.34 vs VA-consensus -$0.12. Management pushed its FCF bridge out by about a year: ~$3B in 2027 (consensus ~$5.3B), ~$6B in 2028 (consensus ~$9.5B), >$10B in 2029 (consensus ~$12.4B). Citi had expected a worse-than-consensus steepening, but guidance came in below even its estimates. Citi moves its price target out a year to $260 at YE27 and keeps its bullish long-term view.

Visa F4Q was in line on top and bottom line, with strong consumer volumes and a pickup in cross-border growth. Value Added Services (~31% of revenue) grew 31%. FY27 guidance is low double-digit adj. cc net revenue growth and low double-digit to low-teens adj. EPS growth, tempered by renewals covering 25% of the book vs a normal 15%-20%. Lower FX volatility and a higher tax rate are headwinds. Buy, $440 TP.

Citi's biotech 3Q26 preview covers AGIO, RYTM and ROIV. AGIO has a mitapivat PDUFA date in sickle cell disease on November 1 and Citi thinks approval is likely (3Q26E $55.1M, $52 TP). RYTM focus is Imcivree scripts in acquired hypothalamic obesity (3Q26E $89.4M, $143 TP). ROIV TP rises $10 to $56 on the early Lisraya launch in dermatomyositis, where Citi sees expectations as low (Citi FY2Q26E $3.0M).

Verizon model updated for 3Q results. Citi cites improving customer acquisition and retention, a $9B cost reduction program, ~$4.4B of cumulative AI fiber and edge contracts, and a millimeter-wave fixed wireless plan that could add 10-15 mm passings. Buy kept, target cut to $53 from $55 partly for a higher cost of capital. Potential Starlink mobile entry is a longer-term valuation risk.

Seagate results beat the Street but missed Citi on exabyte shipments (flat q/q, +21% y/y), while pricing was exceptionally strong. The December guide is very strong. Management says most nearline supply is allocated through CY2028 and demand visibility extends beyond 2030. Estimates rise, but TP is cut to $1,050 from $1,300 on lower peer multiples. Buy reiterated.

S&P Global 3Q revenue was modestly ahead of expectations, with margin strength in Ratings, Energy and Indices driving an earnings beat and another FY26 outlook increase. Management announced a strategic review of Capital IQ and related data assets, which Citi calls the most consequential takeaway. TP rises to $520 from $500, Buy.

Corning beat Street on much better optical performance, partly offset by a slower solar ramp. Revenue guide is slightly above consensus at the midpoint and EPS guide is $0.05 above. Management reaffirmed a 19% revenue CAGR under the Springboard plan. TP falls to $200 from $220 on lower peer multiples (28-29x CY28 vs 32x). Buy maintained.

Datadog 3Q26 preview (reports 11/4): shares are up more than 2x over six months, trade at NTM 18x EV/sales and 68x EV/FCF, and carry a premium to consumption software peers. Citi sees the stock as tactically less compelling into the print but reaffirms Buy on durable ~25%+ revenue CAGR.

Johnson Controls FY26 results and FY27 guidance show solid demand. Record backlog is $23bn (+43% y/y) with 70-80% expected to convert in FY27. Orders are mainly driven by data centers. A restructuring program targets $600mn gross annualized savings by FY29. Citi sees 30%+ operating leverage/EPS growth potential. Rating Neutral, TP $172 from $170.

UPS 3Q adj. EPS of $1.69 beat Citi $1.57 and Street $1.62. Full-year revenue outlook was raised to $92.6bn from $91.2bn and adj. EPS guidance to $7.28. Citi notes a return to volume growth ex-Amazon, industry pricing discipline, lower SMB churn and a favorable revenue-per-piece vs cost-per-piece spread. The 2028 union contract overhang may keep some investors sidelined. Buy, TP $131 from $122.

Ecolab: pricing is running at 5-6%, ahead of costs, though Q4 inflation cost is expected to be higher sequentially. CoolIT and Ovivo are ahead of expectations and the $4bn revenue target by 2030 was reiterated. Heavy Water and Paper is improving. TP rises to $345 from $330, Buy.

Illinois Tool Works 3Q26 showed good demand in capex-driven Test & Measurement/Electronics and Welding, with orders outpacing revenue. Citi expects mixed end markets to limit near-term share price upside. Neutral, TP cut to $310 from $317.

PACCAR: Citi cut 2026E adj. EPS to $5.90 from $6.00 and 2027E to $6.60 from $6.85, and raised 2028E to $7.80 from $7.75. PCAR guided flattish q/q TP&O margins in 4Q. Customer uncertainty on 2027 truck demand is tied to a pending ruling on NCP levels. Neutral, $115 TP.

US application software: Citi expects strong Sep-Q prints from Figma and Shopify and a narrower beat from Klaviyo. For Shopify, Citi is ~300bps above Street on Q3 growth and raises its Q4 revenue growth target above 30%. Klaviyo guide is closer to the pin with a likely cautious FY26 raise.

Novartis 3Q26 read-through for US biopharma: revenues $14.5B and adjusted EPS $2.46. Remibrutinib adds competitive pressure on Biogen in relapsing MS, Kisqali is a headwind for Lilly's Verzenio and Pfizer's Ibrance, and anti-APRIL efficacy pushes Novartis to reassess IgAN positioning as Vertex advances povetacicept. Lp(a) programs are on hold after the pelacarsen CVOT failure, with full data at AHA 11/6-11/9.

Systems software: a hosted discussion with Citi's CISO on the PHP vulnerability headlines supports a lower likelihood of a reactive security budget surge, some scope for renewed web security spending around rogue-agent challenges, and a rising preference to build rather than buy AI defense.

Internet previews for SNAP, DASH, CART, ABNB, BKNG and EXPE focus on AI agents and discovery. Citi's checks show relatively healthy online advertising, marketplace and travel trends, especially in the US, with watch items in the EU (de-minimis changes effective July 1) and Middle East conflict headwinds. A WSJ report (10/26) says DASH may acquire CART.

Digital Asset Monthly: crypto is in a holding pattern. BTC and ETH have drifted lower, total market cap followed, and Bitcoin dominance is steady. BTC ETF flows are modestly positive for the year while ETH has slipped into net outflows. Correlations to equities remain high, and gold and the dollar are the more influential macro anchors. The regulatory direction is positive, including the OCC's finalized stablecoin rules.

Global gas: with markets expecting Middle East escalation (WSJ, Oct 28), Citi estimates winter strips price similar escalation odds and about a one-fourth chance of liquefaction facilities being hit. Citi doubts the facility-hit odds given better Iran-Qatar relations. It sees Henry Hub with stronger risk-adjusted upside than TTF in severe cold, as winter Henry Hub has plunged and managed money net positioning is among the shortest since early 2020.

US economics: consumer confidence rose to 91.7 in October, above expectations, with many consumers still seeing jobs as hard to get, which limits wage pressure. New home sales were close to unchanged in September. Case-Shiller house prices rose 2.1% y/y in August and higher mortgage rates should slow appreciation. Durable goods orders rose 1.8% m/m in September and may be peaking on an annual basis.

High-grade credit: hyperscaler spreads are at their widest since the AI funding wave began, driven by supply uncertainty. Citi sees conditions ripening for a squeeze in the tech/nontech basis as 2027 funding visibility improves. Lower-rated quality curves remain historically compressed, which Citi reads as a reach for yield that leaves investors under-compensated for credit risk.

earnings_insights: Boeing 3Q26 adj. EPS reported -$0.34 vs VA-consensus estimate -$0.12. FCF guidance: ~$3B in 2027 (consensus est ~$5.3B), ~$6B in 2028 (consensus est ~$9.5B), >$10B in 2029 (consensus est ~$12.4B).
Visa F4Q reported in line with expectations. FY27 guidance: low double-digit adj. cc net revenue growth and low double-digit to low-teens adj. EPS growth, in line with expectations.

UPS 3Q reported adj. EPS $1.69 vs Citi est $1.57 and Street est $1.62. Revenue reported $22,853M vs Citi est $22,137M and Street est $22,176M. Full-year adj. EPS guidance $7.28 vs prior Citi est $7.15 and Street est $7.19. 2026 revenue outlook $92.6bn, up from $91.2bn.

S&P Global Citi estimates: 4Q26E total net revenues $3,634M (prior $3,609M), non-GAAP diluted EPS $3.87 (prior $3.99). FY26E non-GAAP EPS $17.74 (prior $17.60) vs outlook of $17.70-$17.95. FY27E non-GAAP EPS $19.94 (prior $20.43) vs Street $20.43 per the estimates table.

Corning results beat Street estimates on optical. Revenue guide is slightly above consensus at the midpoint and EPS guide is $0.05 above consensus. Citi 4QFY26 EPS (PF diluted) estimate $0.91 and FY27 EPS estimate $4.41 per its estimate table.
Seagate results exceeded Street estimates but were below Citi estimates. Exabyte shipments were flat q/q and up 21% y/y. December guide described as extremely strong.

PACCAR Citi estimates: 4Q26 adj. EPS $1.72 (prior $1.81) vs consensus $1.71. 2026 $5.90 (prior $6.00) vs consensus $5.90. 2027 $6.60 (prior $6.85) vs consensus $7.09. 2028 $7.80 (prior $7.75) vs consensus $7.98.
Novartis 3Q26 reported revenues $14.5B (+$58M vs BBG consensus) and adjusted diluted EPS $2.46 (+$0.18 vs consensus), per Citi's read-through.
AGIO Citi 3Q26E revenue estimate $55.1M. RYTM Citi 3Q26E $89.4M. ROIV Citi FY2Q26E Lisraya revenue estimate $3.0M with expectations in the low-to-mid single digits.
Datadog reports C3Q26 on 11/4. Citi illustrates ~1.6% revenue upside from 30% above-commit usage by its largest customers against largely de-risked guide assumptions.
Shopify: Citi expects Q3 growth ~300bps above Street (estimate, not yet reported) and raises its Q4 revenue growth target above 30%.
Johnson Controls FY26 results and FY27 guidance described as continuing solid demand, with 70-80% backlog conversion expected in FY27 and revenue inflection in FY4Q26 on somewhat easier comps.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Stronger than expected but near historically low levels. Many consumers still see jobs as hard to get, which limits wage pressure.
About as expected. Ex-transportation orders and core capital goods orders rose about 0.5%. Growth has slowed vs earlier in the year and AI-related investment growth may slow from very high levels.
Sales remain near levels seen since 2023. Elevated inventory and higher mortgage rates point to lower prices and fewer starts.
Higher mortgage rates reduce affordability and should slow price appreciation in coming months.

crypto_views: Crypto is in a holding pattern. BTC and ETH have drifted down since the last monthly update and total crypto market cap followed, while Bitcoin dominance is broadly steady.
BTC ETF flows are modestly positive for the year. ETH ETF flows have slipped into net outflows. Both have faded from the resumption highlighted last month.
Citi says it stays importantly above the 200-day moving average, where flows tend to be stronger.
Correlations to equities remain high and within their recent range. Gold and the dollar are the more influential macro anchors for BTC.
Regulatory direction is positive and unchanged, including the OCC's finalized stablecoin rules.

trade_ideas.description: Henry Hub gas upside exposure in severe winter 2026-27 cold, favored over TTF on a risk-adjusted basis
trade_ideas.rationale: Winter Henry Hub prices have plunged and managed money net positioning is among the shortest since early 2020.
trade_ideas.risk: Weather outcomes are uncertain, with scenario weights of 34% cold, 33% normal and 33% mild.

risk_factors: Boeing: further rightward shifts in the FCF bridge, with 12 months between rate breaks being the new 6 months.
Verizon: potential Starlink mobile entry is a longer-term industry risk that may restrain valuation.
UPS: the 2028 union contract overhang and any meaningful macro downturn.
PACCAR: customer uncertainty on 2027 truck orders pending a final ruling on NCP levels, and supplier-related issues.
Datadog: sustainability of revenue growth acceleration at a premium valuation.
Durable goods and equipment investment: fading tax incentives and high rates could slow growth from very high levels.
Housing: higher mortgage rates are cutting affordability and demand.
Hyperscaler credit: supply overhang and rating agency concerns about the data center buildout.
Gas markets: Middle East escalation and facility strikes, plus polar vortex weather risk.
vol_and_positioning: Managed money net positioning in Henry Hub is among the shortest since early 2020, which Citi uses to argue for upside skew in severe cold.
Datadog shares are up more than 2x over six months into earnings, with premium valuation vs consumption software peers.
Hyperscaler IG spreads are at their widest since the AI funding wave began. Lower-rated quality curves remain historically compressed.
geopolitical: Market expectation of Middle East conflict escalation (WSJ, Oct 28) is being priced into European gas, with a roughly one-fourth chance of liquefaction facilities being hit implied by winter strips.
Diplomacy to deescalate includes upcoming visits by Qatar, Saudi Arabia and China, alongside Israeli election results.
Citi notes better relations between Iran and Qatar when discussing the odds of liquefaction facilities being hit.
Middle East conflict is cited as a headwind to travel and online trends in the internet previews.
EU de-minimis changes became effective July 1 and are a watch item for e-commerce.

tension_points.bull_case: The North Star driving Citi's bullish long-term view on Boeing appears unchanged and FCF is guided to exceed $10B in 2029.
tension_points.bear_case: Management shifted each year's FCF to the right by about a year, with 2027 and 2028 FCF guided well below consensus.

tension_points.bull_case: Citi sees multiple pathways to outsized topline momentum, including frontier AI demand, AI-native customer ramps and new SKUs, supporting a durable ~25%+ revenue CAGR.
tension_points.bear_case: Shares are up more than 2x over six months at 18x NTM EV/sales and 68x EV/FCF, so the stock looks tactically less compelling into the print.

tension_points.bull_case: Conditions are ripening for a squeeze in the tech/nontech basis as visibility improves for 2027 funding.
tension_points.bear_case: Spreads are at the widest since the AI funding wave began on supply uncertainty, and rating agencies have begun to flag data center buildout risks.

tension_points.bear_case: Citi doubts the facility-hit odds given better Iran-Qatar relations, and diplomacy including Qatar, Saudi Arabia and China visits could deescalate.
